findings.what: A live ping-mode reader still reads dispatch-completions.jsonl and treats c.ok === true as backing proof without isVerifiedLivenessRecord or verifyRecord; it also sits outside liveness-read-choke-point.js SCAN_DIRS.
findings.why: This is a real same-session ok:true dispatch-ledger reader the new structural guard misses. A forged or unsigned row in DISPATCH_LEDGER_DIR can satisfy the §13.6(d) backing-record check and allow subprocess_verified/run_id stamping without a valid origin-proof signature. If verification is added, the reader must also bind the slug through a signed field such as role=skill:<slug> or add skill to the signed field set, because the current check uses the unsigned skill field.

findings.what: The structural guard is token-presence based, not a reliable new-reader catch: OK_PREDICATE only recognizes .ok === true / .ok !== true, and VERIFIES is satisfied by any verifyRecord/isVerifiedLivenessRecord token anywhere in the file.
findings.why: A new same-session reader can read dispatch-completions.jsonl and gate on rec.ok, rec['ok'] === true, a destructured ok, or include a dead import/comment mentioning verifyRecord while still trusting an unsigned record. I confirmed temporary readers with those forms produced zero violations. That means the guard does not actually close the recurrence class it claims to close.

parsed.summary: Fail. The shared liveness helper itself rejects unsigned ok:true by default, the listed main sprint readers mostly route through verification, the cross-session sealed-capsule ceiling is correctly an accepted ED-232 residual, and role-resolver appears env-inert for WARPOS_BOUND_ROLE/WARPOS_ACTOR_KIND. The blocking issue is that the structural guard still misses both an actual same-session reader and straightforward new-reader variants, so the same unsigned ok:true class can be reopened silently.
